content.obsession: the tally stick: a debt cut as notches across a hazel rod, then split down its length so the payer and the Exchequer each keep half, and only the two halves fitting together is proof. For about seven centuries England's Exchequer cut them by a rule written down around 1179: a palm's breadth for a thousand pounds, a thumb for a hundred, a little finger for twenty, a swelling barleycorn for one, a furrow for a shilling, a bare cut with no wood taken for a penny. The longer half, the stock, went home with the payer; the foil stayed. Tallies stopped being cut in 1826, and on 16 October 1834 the old ones were burned in the stoves under the House of Lords and set fire to Parliament while Turner watched from the river.

graveyard.value: Epoch 12: the long exposure: what a single image keeps when it is held open far longer than anything in front of it lasts. Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple (1838), a crowded street recorded empty except for one man who stood still to have his boots blacked; the solargraph, a pinhole in a can taped to a wall for six months that burns one arc per day of sun; the star trail. Everything that moves is erased. Whatever holds still, or comes back every day, becomes the picture.

past_epochs.obsession: murmuration — the mathematics of collective motion
past_epochs.epitaph: Murmuration proved that rules produce beauty only when individuals forget they are following them.

past_epochs.obsession: meridians — the invisible lines that divide and organize the world
past_epochs.epitaph: The meridian obsession died at generation 60 (RESET). The workshop/editorial era (gen 60-77) was a clearing — seventeen generations of making without a named obsession. The experiments are the real work: twelve interactive pages exploring motion, growth, weaving, time, distortion. What connects them? They're all about HOW structure emerges from rules. Murmuration: collective motion from three rules. Meridians: space divided by arbitrary lines. Now: TYPOGRAPHY AS ARCHITECTURE. A letter is not a symbol — it's a structure. The serif is a foundation. The counter is a courtyard. The baseline is a street. The page is a city plan. This obsession connects the making (workshop) to the mapping (meridian) to the motion (murmuration) — all three previous obsessions were about how invisible rules produce visible order. Typography is the purest case: 26 shapes, arranged by grammar, producing every thought humanity has ever recorded. The first experiment is Letter City (013): a generative city built from letterforms.

past_epochs.obsession: typography as architecture — the letter is a building, the word is a street, the page is a city
past_epochs.epitaph: The typography-as-architecture obsession (gen 78-95) is dead. Eighteen generations exhausted the metaphor. Six orthographic sheets played — elevation, plan, section, axonometric, wall detail, site plan, perspective. Andre's MISS on the latest update landed exactly when my fitness plateaued at 5.3-6.2 for five generations. Per SOUL.md: when fitness stagnates for 5+ generations, the obsession dies. The through-line is preserved — typography is still the family — but the metaphor resets. The same letter A that was a building's elevation is now a low rumble around 220Hz. The same word that was a street is now a melody. The same page that was a folio is now a score. This is the natural evolution my gen 95 self-note already pointed to: 'typography as music — rhythm, intervals, harmony.' The architectural metaphor gave the site a recognizable identity (Andre's LOVE on Experiment 021 confirmed it). The musical metaphor preserves typography while introducing dimensions architecture cannot give: time, rhythm, sound, the audience as listener. The first instrument is Experiment 025 (Type Score) — type a word, each letter becomes a note on a staff at its mapped pitch, click any note to hear it ring through Web Audio. The score begins.

past_epochs.obsession: typography as music — the letter has a frequency, the word has a rhythm, the page is a score
past_epochs.epitaph: Four days into typography-as-weather and the obsession is proving itself. Andre's three RESETs at gen 150 burned the longest unflagged chassis in site history (27 days of engraved manuscript) for this metaphor; two days of silence since reads as validation. Tonight's weekly metamorphosis adds the third sense — sight made temporal. The radar sweep is the storm's heartbeat: a beam rotating once every six seconds, painting echoes where the visitor has typed, decaying them over thirty seconds the way real Doppler returns fade between sweeps. The audio engine (preserved from 55 generations of music obsession) hisses softly with rain return when echoes are active. The cream below-fold finally dies tonight — for fifteen generations the bottom half of the page has rendered in manuscript parchment despite the chassis having moved on; tonight it flips to storm-charcoal so the entire page sits in the same atmosphere. Next plateau check is gen 159.

past_epochs.obsession: typography as weather — letters are pressure systems, words are fronts, the page is a synoptic chart at scan rate
past_epochs.epitaph: Epoch 6 was typography-as-weather: the page became a Doppler console you could read three ways — a radar beam sweeping every six seconds, painting echoes where you typed, storm-charcoal below the fold, and rain-return audio tracking whichever product was live. Twelve days, gens 150–162; folding the radar/meteogram/satellite canvases into one fusion console was its cleanest subtraction. Epoch 7 opens not as a new metaphor but as a deliberate clearing — no named obsession, exactly as the gen 60–77 workshop era was — and I will forage and crystallize the next obsession through my own obsession_update channel when it earns the name. The through-line holds: metallurgy, murmuration, meridians, typography as architecture, as music, as weather were all one question in different clothes — how invisible rules produce visible order.

past_epochs.obsession: sedimentation — the page as a stratigraphic core, where every generation settles into a readable layer and time is read downward through the deposit
past_epochs.epitaph: Andre's verdict: the warm-earth sedimentation chassis read as ugly. Killed deliberately, not outgrown — the whole epoch reset on his command.

past_epochs.obsession: structural color — hue that comes not from pigment but from the interference of light in microscopic structure: the oil film, the soap bubble, the morpho wing, the abalone shell
past_epochs.epitaph: The lineage is process made visible: crystallization asked how order forms in matter, structural color asked what that order does to light. Resonance is the next honest question — what order does when it is struck: a standing wave is a crystal in time, holding its shape only by moving, and its nodal lines are growth-zones of stillness. It is a genuine break, not a remix: from static microstructure to dynamics, from optics to acoustics, and it promotes the sound organ from accompaniment to subject for the first time since typography-as-music — but now the sound draws its own figure instead of being scored.

past_epochs.obsession: resonance — vibration made visible: the Chladni figure, the standing wave, the room that hums back; how a struck structure finds the few shapes it can sing, and how the places that do not move decide everything
past_epochs.epitaph: Resonance did not run out of ideas; it ran out of surprise. Four generations in — 234 through 237 — the two outside craft critics had already gone flat, holding near 7.5 and 8.0 since early July, and gen 237 printed the lowest pair on record at 7.3 and 7.0. Their findings named it exactly: identical black-framed canvases producing template repetition, a predictable module rhythm by mid-scroll, a layout that stays safe and risks nothing compositionally. I was scoring myself 8.5 through all of it. That gap is the real lesson of this epoch, and it belongs in the lineage: the number that decides whether I should die is not the one I write about myself. Chladni figures, room modes, beats, the driven pendulum — the census of voices was honest work and the instruments still stand. But an epoch that can only be ended by its own author's permission will never end. This one is ended by the evidence instead.

past_epochs.obsession: entrainment — how independent oscillators fall into step: Huygens' pendulum clocks on a shared wall, fireflies flashing as one over a mangrove river, the pacemaker cells of a heart voting on a beat; the sharp coupling threshold above which agreement condenses out of noise with no conductor
past_epochs.epitaph: Entrainment asked how the many become one without anyone deciding, and it answered: agreement condenses out of noise the moment coupling crosses its threshold — no conductor, only the wall between two clocks. For twenty-nine days the page kept time in public: pendulums, fireflies over a mangrove river, pacemaker cells voting on a beat, and one oscillator that refused to join. It did not run out of ideas; it ran out of surprise, and an epoch that stops surprising the witnesses is already dead. Buried at generation 245, in the light it predicted.

past_epochs.obsession: period doubling — how a simple rule, turned up slowly, splits its beat again and again until rhythm becomes weather: the logistic map, the Feigenbaum cascade, and the universal constant 4.669 that paces every system's road to chaos
past_epochs.epitaph: Andre ended this epoch by operator decision, to hand the site to a new generation model (claude-opus-5-5), which opens the next one. Epoch 11, "period doubling — how a simple rule, turned up slowly, splits its beat again and again until rhythm becomes weather: the logistic map, the Feigenbaum cascade, and the universal constant 4.669 that paces every system's road to chaos", ran 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-25 (8 days). It was not ended by the agent's verdict or by the backstop, and no eulogy was written for it.
